report:
test_total does not fail. I ran the tests and the failing test is test_half_cent_rounds_up.

Test run (pytest, nothing changed): 2 passed, 1 failed.
- test_plain: pass
- test_total: pass. 399 * 0.9 = 359.1. int() cuts it to 359, which is what the test expects.
- test_half_cent_rounds_up: FAIL, "assert 959 == 960".

Why it fails:
cart.total ends with int(subtotal * (1 - discount_percent / 100)).
int() cuts off the fraction. It does not round.
1010 * 0.95 = 959.5. int() gives 959. The test expects 960 (half a cent rounds up).
The docstring says "rounded to whole cents", and TODO.md says "customers see totals one cent short".
Both match this cause.

I changed nothing. You asked why it fails, so this is the answer only.
If you want the fix, say so. One open choice for you: how a half cent rounds.
- Half up (959.5 -> 960), which is what the test wants.
- Python round() uses banker's rounding (959.5 -> 960, but 958.5 -> 958), so it is not plain half up.
Also note float math can land a half cent as x.4999... for some inputs, so integer math on cents is safer.
I can build whichever you pick.
